title: Eskista (Ethiopian shoulder dance)
summary: Eskista is the shoulder dance of the Amhara and Tigray peoples of Ethiopia and Eritrea. The dancer keeps her feet almost still and moves only her shoulders, chest and neck, shivering and rolling in rhythm to the drum and the singer, so that every part of the upper body seems to follow its own beat.
howToPlay: The dancer stands in her white dress with a woven border. Five places are lit: Left and Right shoulders, Chest, Back and Neck.
A ring closes on a place when that part of the body should move. Strike it as the ring closes and the dancer answers.
Start with the three-beat shoulder shiver, then try the chest and neck figure.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the tradition, not transcriptions.
heritageNote: Eskista is danced at weddings and celebrations. Each region has its own style, from the fast shoulder shivers of the north to the slow chest rolls of Gondar.
